title: Cross-method video Mirror marginal-byte and decode-speed tournament
hypothesis: Across matched video contents and coded-rate points, Mirror methods that compress model/code state improve marginal quality-per-byte without increasing decode speed or peak VRAM cost relative to native codec controls.
physical_object: Comparable trained video INRs/codecs with actual encoded bitstreams and matching scene/frame contents.
mirror_coordinate: Method family selector across frame/segment/rate View codes.
logical_multiplicity: Comparable useful frame/video functions under matched bitstream and decoder budgets.

development.selection_metric: Not run; no two comparable native outcomes.

storage.authority: actual embedded bitstream plus decoder/model payload bytes

success_gate: Not evaluated; identical content and bitrate grid across at least two native codec families required.
blockers: Only one comparable point exists: MA-939 HNeRV Bunny serialized embedding frontier; it is model-state payload, not an entropy-coded bitstream.
No NerVast, DCVC-UF, DCVC-RT, or DCMVC official weights/bitstreams in the workspace.
No CUDA/NVIDIA for peak VRAM and matched decode FPS.
boundaries: Do not compare unrelated contents or incomparable rate points.
Do not treat serialized neural payload as bpp or a bitstream tournament.
